description: Single-panel figure rendered entirely as Table 3, described by the caption as the microstructural parameters (α_p, Lt(t), V_γ, εγ, εα) of the investigated steels under different T_A and T_B conditions. Columns are: Alloy | Parameter | α_p (%) | Lt(t) (nm) | SD (Lt(t)) | V_γ (%) | ε_γ (%) | ε_α (%). Rows are grouped by alloy, two or three austempering conditions each: S1 (T_A 1150 °C with T_B 350 °C and 300 °C), S2 (1150/350, 1150/300), S3 (1220/350, 1220/270), S4 (1150/350, 1150/320, 1250/350) and S5 (1150/365, 1150/335); 11 data rows in total. α_p is given once per alloy and is "–" for S1 and S2, 8.2% for S3, "<1.0" for S4 and S5. Lt(t) is 34–41 nm at the lower T_B and 55–68 nm at the higher T_B; SD(Lt(t)) is larger at high T_B (15–28) than at low T_B (10–14). V_γ reaches 34% for S1–S3 at the higher T_B versus 27–29% at lower T_B, and stays ≤29% for S4 and S5 (lowest 19% for S5 at 335 °C). ε_γ spans 0.31–0.58% and ε_α 0.33–0.60%. The table demonstrates that lowering the austempering temperature refines bainitic lath thickness and narrows its spread, whereas the higher T_B raises the retained-austenite fraction most strongly in the higher-alloyed steels.

subfigures.description: Full rendered data table (Table 3) with columns Alloy, Parameter, α_p (%), Lt(t) (nm), SD (Lt(t)), V_γ (%), ε_γ (%) and ε_α (%), containing 11 data rows for alloys S1–S5 under their respective T_A/T_B (austenitizing/austempering) conditions. All cell values legible; α_p is populated only once per alloy.

observations.observation: The table lists five alloys (S1, S2, S3, S4, S5) with 11 condition rows: S1 and S2 have two rows each (T_B 350 °C and 300 °C at T_A 1150 °C), S3 two rows (1220 °C with T_B 350 °C and 270 °C), S4 three rows (1150/350, 1150/320, 1250/350) and S5 two rows (1150/365, 1150/335).
α_p (%) is reported only once per alloy and only for some alloys: "–" (dash, not reported) for S1 and S2, 8.2 for S3, "<1.0" for S4 and "<1.0" for S5; the remaining α_p cells are blank.

Lt(t) values are 34, 40, 41 and 36 nm at the low-T_B conditions (S2 at 300 °C; S3 at 270 °C; S5 at 335 °C; S4 at 320 °C) and 55, 56, 58, 68, 55 and 58 nm at the high-T_B conditions (S1 350; S2 350; S3 350; S4 350 and S4 1250/350; S5 365).
SD(Lt(t)) is 23, 28, 23, 18, 18 and 15 for the high-T_B rows and 11, 11, 10, 12 and 14 for the low-T_B rows, i.e. systematically larger at the higher austempering temperature.

V_γ is 34% for S1, S2 and S3 at their high T_B, and 27%, 29% and 29% respectively at their lower T_B; for S4 and S5 V_γ lies between 19% and 29%, the lowest value in the table being 19% for S5 at T_B 335 °C.

ε_γ (%) ranges from 0.31 (S4, 1150/350) to 0.58 (S4, 1150/320), and ε_α (%) from 0.33 (S3, 1220/270) to 0.60 (S4, 1150/320), so the largest phase-resolved micro-strains both occur for S4 at T_A 1150 °C/T_B 320 °C.
The caption states that the table gives the microstructural parameters α_p, Lt(t), V_γ, εγ and εα of the investigated steels under different T_A and T_B conditions.

The citing text states that in steels S1, S2 and S3 bainitic transformation at the higher T_B (350 °C) gave V_γ up to 34%, more pronouncedly incomplete than at lower T_B where V_γ ranged between 27% and 29%, while in S4 and S5 the effect of T_B on V_γ was more limited, remaining below 30% — all consistent with the table values.

The citing text states that average Lt(t) values range from 34 to 41 nm at low T_B and 55–68 nm at high T_B, and that for S4 Lt(t) remained within 56–58 nm regardless of austenitization temperature (1150 vs 1250 °C) — matching rows S4 1150/350 (56 nm) and S4 1250/350 (58 nm).

The citing text states that at high T_B the standard deviation of Lt(t) increased, indicating a broader range of bainitic thicknesses, most pronounced in S1, S2 and S3, lower in S4 and negligible in S5 — in agreement with the SD column (23/28/23 for S1–S3 at 350 °C vs 11/11/10 at lower T_B).

The citing text states that for S3 at T_B 270 °C the phase-resolved micro-strain differed markedly between γr and bainitic ferrite (εγ: 0.54% vs εα: 0.33%), consistent with pronounced strain partitioning; the table shows exactly εγ 0.54% and εα 0.33% for S3 at 1220/270 °C.

A different citing sentence reports for the 270 °C condition a higher average 'εγ (0.33%)' compared with the 'ferritic phases (0.58%)' and, in a separate sentence, gives εγ: 0.51% and εα: 0.45% with 19% retained austenite for T_B 335 °C; the first statement contradicts the table (εγ 0.54%, εα 0.33%) and appears to have the two phases swapped, whereas the 0.51/0.45/19% values match the S5 335 °C row.
